questions: Section 10 refers private aviation to underwriting judgement, and a referral is available here. For a private pilot with 1,342 total hours, flying 75 hours a year with no aerobatics, on a 30-year term for $1,000,000: how is the aviation risk handled in practice - a debit (and if so, more or less than the 50 default for an unreferred file), a flat extra, an aviation exclusion rider, or no charge?

Section 11 refers a recent motoring conviction to underwriting judgement. This applicant has a DUI conviction in 2024, roughly two years before this application, alongside 2 moving violations in the last 3 years, with normal liver enzymes and no alcohol history. Does a DUI that recent mean the file is postponed until more time has elapsed, rated with a heavier charge than the tabled 50, or rated at the tabled 50 as written?

Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors to underwriting judgement. This applicant presents untreated blood pressure 147/83, total cholesterol 268 with a ratio of 5.3, and A1c 6.8 with no diabetes diagnosis, all together. Is that combination handled simply by adding the individual table debits, or does the co-occurrence of these three factors carry an additional loading or change the decision?
